newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Cape Town firms pledge cash to Olympic bid.
newsitem.headline: Cape Town firms pledge cash to Olympic bid.

text.p: A group of Cape Town companies said on Thursday that they had pledged 5.5 million rand ($1.2 million) to the South African city's bid to host the 2004 Olympic Games.
The companies include mutual assurer Sanlam, Engen, Pepkor, Boland Bank, Shoprite and Nasionale Pers.
Sanlam chairman Marinus Daling said the firms were backing the bid in the belief that holding the games would reap economic benefits such as increased levels of infrastructure investment and tourism.
"Together this will result in the creation of a large number of permanent new jobs, which will directly or indirectly benefit all the people of our region," he added.
Cape Town, shortlisted with Buenos Aires, Stockholm, Rome and Athens, will hear on September 6 whether it will become the first African venue for the Olympic Games.

Cape Town's bid committee estimates the Games could inject up to 30 billion rand into the national economy, much of it into the city's local economy, create up to 100,000 permanent jobs and put the city firmly on the world tourism map
